messages.author: 6e0bce06355e4e6c
messages.subject: User-defined truncated lognormal distribution
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to use STAN for a model that runs -much- too slow in BUGS to be of any use. This model requires a user-defined distribution that I have currently implemented in WB-DEV. It's a truncated lognormal distribution with only one parameter (tau); the other parameter (mu) is set internally to impose that the (posterior) expectation of the distribution stays equal to 1. During estimation, the set of parameters that use this distribution as its prior can be further constrained to an exact average of 1, but this is not even necessary. Right now, to keep things simple, I have used pre-determined truncation boundaries so mu can be set via a polynomial approximation that only depends on tau. In general, a more complicated function that depends on the truncation boundaries as well as tau needs to be solved to zero, but this is not required for my model.

Hence my question, how difficult would it be to implement the more simple solution (with fixed truncation boundaries) in STAN?

Best,
Marcel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] User-defined truncated lognormal distribution
parts: On Wed, Feb 6, 2013 at 5:20 AM, Marcel Jonker <mfjo...@hotmail.com> wrote:

Dear all,

I would like to use STAN for a model that runs -much- too slow in BUGS to be of any use. This model requires a user-defined distribution that I have currently implemented in WB-DEV. It's a truncated lognormal distribution with only one parameter (tau); the other parameter (mu) is set internally to impose that the (posterior) expectation of the distribution stays equal to 1. During estimation, the set of parameters that use this distribution as its prior can be further constrained to an exact average of 1, but this is not even necessary. Right now, to keep things simple, I have used pre-determined truncation boundaries so mu can be set via a polynomial approximation that only depends on tau. In general, a more complicated function that depends on the truncation boundaries as well as tau needs to be solved to zero, but this is not required for my model.

Hence my question, how difficult would it be to implement the more simple solution (with fixed truncation boundaries) in STAN?

You should be able to do this. tau should be a parameter, mu should be a transformed parameter. The lognormal distribution has its cdf, which means that you can use it for truncated distributions. (see pg. 201 of v1.1.1 of the manual) At the moment, if you want to use truncated distributions, you can't vectorize the call, but that sounds like the least of your worries. Hopefully we'll have vectorized truncated calls in the Stan modeling language soon.
